lore_anchors.definition: A member of the "Heart" generation whose destiny is permanently and inextricably "coiled" (蟠) with a higher power, such as a Siming.
A cryptic epithet for a very powerful Siming from the White Jade Capital, whose true name is too dangerous to speak aloud.
A notoriously painful and vile ascension technique from the Ao-Jing Sect, involving self-mutilation and corruption.
A class of high-dimensional, god-like entities that oversee specific aspects of reality and are often the objects of worship for various cults.
The original Chinese term for the entire xianxia genre. In this novel, it is revealed to be a literal cultivation path that directly opposes the Zuowandao's method of cultivating the false.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the "One Above the Three Bodies"?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is a cryptic and dangerous epithet used by Zhuge Yuan to refer to a powerful Siming (司命) from the White Jade Capital. Speaking its true name would supposedly invite its attention, which is why he uses a vague term.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why do the Zuowandao hate Heart-Elements so much?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Zhuge Yuan deduces that it is because the Heart-Element's unique power—making their own beliefs and hallucinations real—is a natural, hard counter to the Zuowandao's cultivation method of "replacing the true with the false."

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the Heart-Element's cultivation method?
cultural_notes_faq.a: While not yet fully revealed, Zhuge Yuan mentions a forgotten book that details a technique for controlling a Heart-Element's excess innate One Qi. He concludes that this technique is called "Cultivating the True" (修真), a direct counter to the Zuowandao's "Cultivating the False" (修假).
